resolutions: An impersonal patientive begins with the exact owner-issued impersonal VNC Result.
The exact typed nonactive core supplies the patientive Source rather than a raw stem string.
The active Source, class, valence, participants, impersonal operation, internal boundaries, and vowel quantity remain attached.
Copied Results, formulas, surfaces, and example identity cannot authorize the route.
The patientive names a result or product rather than the agent who performs the event.
English participle language is reading help and never grammar authority.
A typed lō boundary loses final ō and retains l automatically.
The lō patientive receives tli class without a manual class choice.
Any root-plus-ya realization has already been decided by the owner-issued VNC Result and is not asked again in Lesson 38.
Earlier inherent, tla-impersonal, and nonactive layers remain in the full Source analysis.
Any compatible typed Source receives the lō rule without Canvas-example membership.
Narrow lō meanings and unusual vowel realizations require typed lexical Source or context.
A typed ō boundary loses the complete nonactive suffix automatically.
A typed o-hua boundary loses the complete extended nonactive material automatically.
The ō and o-hua patientives preserve the exact active-to-impersonal Source chain.
Changes such as e to a, ti to ch, and ci to x remain typed morphological or lexical analyses rather than spelling guesses.
The compositional patientive reading remains available while narrow readings require typed Source or context.
Changing to another compatible Source shape preserves eligibility, while changing owner identity or required typed grammar facts blocks the route.
Groups 1 through 3 add no stem whitelist, duplicate root-plus-ya control, final-letter authority, copied-Result authority, formula authority, or surface authority.
A typed hua boundary is removed automatically from an exact impersonal Result.
Preceding long ī shortens to i only through the typed nonactive Source analysis, while other vowel behavior remains owner-issued.
The hua patientive receives tl class without a manual class choice.
An alternative lō formation requires its own exact owner-issued VNC Result rather than a patientive-stage switch.
The productive final-i or final-o Source lattice may expose a typed hua-lō nonactive possibility without using an example-stem whitelist.
A typed hua-lō boundary loses only final ō and retains the inner hua plus l structure.
The user cannot manually choose which hua-lō layer to delete, and final letters cannot reconstruct the layered Source.
An exact reflexive or reciprocal impersonal Source carries shuntline ne into the patientive automatically.
Any surviving nonspecific human or nonhuman projective object remains alongside ne as tē or tla.
A projective object may distinguish passive from impersonal structure; without one, genuine surface ambiguity remains visible.
Passive and impersonal analyses retain distinct owner-issued Result identities even where their surface patientives overlap.
Groups 4 through 6 add no manual vowel, noun-class, deletion-layer, or ne choice and no Source reconstruction from a nounstem surface.
A projective impersonal patientive retains its nonspecific nonhuman direct object as tla.
With a surviving nonspecific human recipient, the direct-patient tla remains after tē as the typed double-object sequence tē+tla.
Participant roles come from the exact captured VNC object topology and are not reconstructed from prefix order.
The projective lō family loses final ō and retains l while keeping tla or tē+tla.
The projective ō family removes the complete typed nonactive suffix while keeping tla or tē+tla.
The projective hua family removes typed hua while preserving the active Source vowel analysis.
A phonemically long vowel in the active verbstem remains long after hua deletion.
In the productive projective final-a pattern, active a becomes ī before hua and is short i after hua is removed.
The final-a hua route requires both the typed projective-nonhuman analysis and the final-a Source shape; shape alone does not license it.
Compositional patient readings remain available while narrow meanings and homophony require typed Source or context.
Groups 7 through 9 add no object-carrier, object-placement, vowel-behavior, or example-stem choice and no formula or surface authority.
A single-object active Source with nonspecific human tē does not pass directly into an impersonal patientive.
The human-object Source first forms its typed passive, promotes the human patient, and then impersonalizes that passive.
Impersonalization removes the promoted passive subject and supplies tla while the patientive referent remains human.
The complete active to passive to impersonalized-passive sequence remains attached to the exact owner-issued VNC Result.
Human-source lō patientives lose final ō and retain l after the passive and impersonal stages.
Human-source ō patientives remove the complete typed ō suffix after the same voice sequence.
Human-source hua patientives remove hua and inherit the typed vowel behavior, including ī to i where licensed.
The corresponding passive patientive remains grammatically distinct even when translation values overlap.
A tla patientive with a human referent and a homonymous tla patientive with a nonhuman referent retain different typed Source histories.
Canvas examples prove each productive family and never gate compatible unlisted verbstems.
Rare human-naming tē patientives are automatic only when typed lexical Source analysis licenses the exception.
The attested huica and ilpi exceptions do not expose a general tē-retention picker or authorize unrelated Sources.
Carrier, voice path, participant promotion and deletion, referent, suffix removal, and exception status are derived rather than manual.
Groups 10 through 12 add no active-to-impersonal shortcut, referent inference from surface, stem whitelist, copied-Result authority, formula authority, or surface authority.
In the nāhuatiā contrast, typed active human or nonhuman valence settles the patientive automatically.
When the same typed human-object Source genuinely supports both readings, the user chooses regular human tla or anomalous nonhuman or abstract tē.
The exceptional tē reading is lexical analysis and never licenses a general productive route or blocks an ordinary unlisted patientive.
The machtiā contrast keeps single-object impersonal and double-object passive Source histories distinct.
Tē and tla alone decide neither transitivity nor the patientive referent.
Typed lexical vowel quantity remains exact in icnēliā and tlāuhtiā contrast forms.
A patientive and an active-action nounstem remain distinct constructions and owner-issued Results even when English translates them alike.
English translation cannot merge, select, or authorize either grammatical analysis.
A compound patientive captures the exact owner-issued VNC Result, Source analysis, embed, matrix, and internal boundaries.
The user chooses the compound relation only when the typed compound Source leaves adverbial versus incorporated-object interpretation open.
Nahuatl constituent order remains embed before matrix and is never a manual choice.
English matrix-before-embed reversal for an incorporated-object reading is guidance only and cannot alter the Source.
The compound Source is never flattened into a string or reconstructed from the patientive surface.
Compatible typed compound Sources remain productive and Canvas examples never form a whitelist.
Copied VNC Results and a compound-relation choice on a noncompound Source are rejected.
Compound patientives preserve scalar and paradigm equivalence through the same canonical operation.
The patientive referent and compound-relation controls appear only for their genuine typed choices.
Groups 13 through 15 add no prefix-only inference, translation authority, example gate, copied-Result authority, formula authority, or surface authority.
A patientive NNC Result can serve as the matrix of a compound only through its exact owner-issued Result identity.
The patientive matrix preserves its complete VNC ancestry, Source analysis, noun class, and morphemic boundaries through capture and continuation.
The user supplies the typed nounstem embed and chooses its genuine grammatical relation to the patientive matrix.
Nahuatl constituent order remains embed before matrix and the patientive matrix governs the Result noun class automatically.
Boundary behavior is derived by the canonical compound owner rather than entered as a separate choice.
Changing the compatible typed embed or verbstem Source shape preserves route eligibility without a witnessed-stem gate.
A compositional compound reading remains available while narrow lexical meanings require typed Source or context.
Copied Results, JSON lookalikes, nounstem strings, formulas, surfaces, and the wrong Result family cannot authorize continuation.
Section 39.6 remains responsible for the reverse patientive-as-embed arrangement.
Group 16 adds no matrix-identity choice, boundary choice, class choice, example gate, copied-Result authority, formula authority, or surface authority.
